intro_html: This one is sweet, savory, and about as easy as dinner gets. Tender teriyaki pork over rice with broccoli and onion gives you 58 grams of protein a bowl for around $4.14 (at everyday cost). Fourteen servings means you cook once and eat well all week.
cost_closing_html: About $4.14 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each serving lands near 565 calories with 58 grams of protein.
upsell_html: Sweet, simple, and satisfying. This is comfort food that respects your budget. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Bottled teriyaki sauce carries the whole dish, but it is the priciest item here. Compare the store brand against the name brand, since they taste about the same in the slow cooker.
Stretch it with a little honey and broth. A splash of each thins the sauce so one bottle coats the entire batch.
Buy onions by the bag when you batch cook. They keep for weeks in a cool spot and cost about 30 cents each that way.
make_it: Place the pork tenderloin in the slow cooker and scatter the sliced onion around it.
Pour the teriyaki sauce, chicken broth, honey, and garlic over the top.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork pulls apart.
Shred the pork and stir it back into the sauce with the onions.
Steam the broccoli florets until just tender.
Serve over cooked white rice and divide into containers.
